projectDescription: CARL is a dog-sized, 12-DOF biologically inspired quadruped robot built on a 24V power system and modular electronics. Featuring ROS2 compatibility, the platform utilizes an NVIDIA Orin NX, Raspberry Pi 4, and 360-degree LiDAR to manage autonomous navigation and complex limb actuation across its modular chassis.

imagePromptSnapshot.description:
Project idea: Design an open-source, biologically inspired embodied autonomous quadruped research robot named CARL.

Requirements:
- Dog-sized platform (50-70 cm body length)
- 12 DOF legs (3 DOF per leg)
- Modular electronics and actuators
- NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX as main computer
- STM32 motor control network over CAN-FD
- ROS2 compatible
- Intel RealSense D455
- OAK-D Lite
- 360° LiDAR
- 9-axis IMU
- Foot force sensors
- Battery powered (24V Li-ion)

The robot should support:
- autonomous navigation
- visual SLAM
- embodied AI
- self-calibration
- lifelong learning
- digital twin synchronization
- future tactile skin integration

Generate:
- complete CAD concept
- exploded assembly
- BOM
- wiring diagram
- PCB architecture
- power budget
- communication architecture
- actuator recommendations
- manufacturing plan
- estimated cost

Design notes: dog-sized platform, 12 DOF legs, modular electronics, ROS2 compatible, 24V power system, biologically inspired

Electrical components (current): Main Compute Board (module, 70x45x15mm); 4x mcu: Front Right Limb Controller, Front Left Limb Controller, Rear Right Limb Controller, Rear Left Limb Controller; 4x sensor: Primary Vision Sensor, Navigation Vision Sensor, 360 Degree LiDAR, 9-Axis IMU; Front Left Hip Joint (actuator, 85x85x45mm); 24V Power Distribution (power, 100x80x20mm)

Mechanical/structural parts (current): 2x structural: Main Chassis Frame, FL Upper Leg; 10x 3d_printed: Orin NX Mount, LiDAR Mast, FL Hip Motor Mount, Depth Sensor Mount +6 more; 2x misc: M3x12mm Bolts, M3 Heat Set Inserts

originalPrompt:
Design an open-source, biologically inspired embodied autonomous quadruped research robot named CARL.

Requirements:
- Dog-sized platform (50-70 cm body length)
- 12 DOF legs (3 DOF per leg)
- Modular electronics and actuators
- NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX as main computer
- STM32 motor control network over CAN-FD
- ROS2 compatible
- Intel RealSense D455
- OAK-D Lite
- 360° LiDAR
- 9-axis IMU
- Foot force sensors
- Battery powered (24V Li-ion)

The robot should support:
- autonomous navigation
- visual SLAM
- embodied AI
- self-calibration
- lifelong learning
- digital twin synchronization
- future tactile skin integration

Generate:
- complete CAD concept
- exploded assembly
- BOM
- wiring diagram
- PCB architecture
- power budget
- communication architecture
- actuator recommendations
- manufacturing plan
- estimated cost
plan: - Select high-torque brushless DC (BLDC) motors with integrated cycloidal or planetary gearboxes for 3 DOF leg joints.- Utilize custom CNC-machined aluminum or high-strength carbon fiber chassis plates to house the 24V Li-ion battery and internal electronics.- Implement an STM32-based distributed motor control network via CAN-FD for low-latency gait execution.- Integrate the NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX as the primary compute node for SLAM, navigation, and neural network inference.- 3D print protective enclosures, sensor mounts for D455/OAK-D, and leg cable conduits for durability and cable management.- Deploy custom foot force sensor assemblies using piezoresistive arrays or load cells at the contact points for ground reaction force feedback.

assumptions: Access to a 24V high-current DC power supply
Prior experience with 3D printer slicing (PETG profiles)
Basic understanding of CAN bus and I2C protocols
ROS2 Humble or later environment configured on development machine

subSteps.title: 3D print chassis mounts and structural components using PETG
Install heat-set inserts into leg components
Verify chassis plate dimensions and mounting hole alignment
Solder power leads to 24V distribution module
Construct wiring harness for 24V to 5V step-down
Prepare CAN-FD data lines for limb controllers
Perform continuity check on all logic power rails
Flash firmware to MCU nodes and verify CAN bus communication
Initialize I2C bus and verify IMU sensor data streams
Calibrate joint actuators and verify PWM range limits
Validate lidar sensor UART connection in ROS2
Mount MCU controllers and IMU to chassis base plate
Assemble upper leg structure with hip motor
Install LiDAR mast and sensor array to chassis
Mount computing modules and cable manage the chassis
